newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Gonzalez taunts government on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Gonzalez taunts government on Cuba.

text.p: Spanish opposition leader Felipe Gonzalez taunted the conservative government on Friday for its get-tough policy on Cuba, saying Madrid's European partners would be only too happy to exploit any vacuum in economic ties.
Gonzalez, speaking to reporters, also said most European Union members consider the terms of Spain's recent proposal for a common European policy on Cuba "excessive".

"There are some European leaders who will be very amused because they know the space this political fumble is going to open for the other countries' investments is going to be exploited by some of our European partners," Gonzalez said.

Government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez, speaking to reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting, dismissed Gonzalez's remarks. He said Spain's policy was shared by "the entire civilised world, except Gonzalez".
Spain has had historically close ties to Cuba and is a major investor in the Caribbean island.
The new conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has taken a tougher line on Cuba than its predecessor, which was headed by Socialist leader Gonzalez for nearly 14 years.
Earlier this month, Spain presented a proposal to the European Union for a common policy on Cuba along the lines of its own.

The document called on Cuba to sign international human rights conventions, reform its penal code, establish an independent judiciary, cease discrimination against political dissidents, free political prisoners, allow freedom of movement and free activity of unions and non-governmental organisations.
The Spanish daily El Pais reported on Friday that Ireland, which currently holds the European Union presidency, was seeking to tone down the document.
A Foreign Ministry official denied the report, saying there were no substantive differences in the Spanish proposal and a document revised by Ireland which is circulating among EU members.
Spanish government officials said on Friday they were satisfied with the European Union response to their initiative and did not indicate any differences of opinion.

Spain shares European Union opposition to a U.S. embargo of Cuba and the U.S. Helms-Burton legislation which allows lawsuits to be filed in U.S. courts against foreign firms that buy or sell properties of U.S. citizens seized by the Cuban government after the 1959 revolution.
